context: During analysis of a suspicious process-injection incident, we noted that a process named "powershell.exe" (PID 4656) was started with a long base-64-encoded command at 2024-06-26T15:49:41Z. This activity is part of a series of "Suspicious process injection observed" alerts that suggest the injected code might be reaching out to an external host.
question: In the earlier "Suspicious process injection observed" alert that occurred just before the PowerShell execution, which external IP address is listed as being contacted?
solution: Alert at 2024-07-04 22:35:01.343148+00:00 shows a suspicious process injection tied to user account with AadUserId `12185914-91dd-4fb9-94f9-3252203b0426`.
Just moments earlier, at 2024-07-04 22:35:00.869748+00:00, a related suspicious process injection was observed communicating with IP Address `72.5.72.208`.

context: During investigation, we saw user "nathans" (SID S-1-5-21-1240151660-3534038288-105586567-4122) using host "vnevado-win11a" where a process named "notepad.exe" (PID 8932, created 2024-06-26 15:49:51 UTC) was involved in a suspicious code-injection event. Immediately afterward, another alert for the same technique (process injection) was raised, indicating that a different process became the recipient of the injected code.
question: What is the executable file name of the process that was identified as the injection target in the follow-up alert?
solution: Alert 1 – Suspicious process injection: the target process had field ProcessId__CreatedTimeUtc__CommandLine with value `8932__2024-06-26t15:49:51.3043595z__"notepad.exe"`, showing that process ID 8932 (notepad.exe, created 2024-06-26T15:49:51Z) received injected code.

Alert 2 – Suspicious process injection: the injecting or injected process is identified by field ExtractedFileName with value `powershell.exe`, indicating PowerShell was involved in the code-injection activity.

context: Microsoft Defender has raised an alert for a suspicious process injection. During the investigation, it was observed that user account 'nathans' (AadUserId 12185914-91dd-4fb9-94f9-3252203b0426, SID S-1-5-21-1240151660-3534038288-105586567-4122) executed an obfuscated PowerShell command from a file named powershell.exe (PID 4656). Shortly afterwards, the process notepad.exe (PID 8932) was also started. Network traffic was noted toward the external IP address 72.5.72.208, and the script attempted to download content from https://wcdstaticfilesprdeus.blob.core.windows.net/wcdstaticfiles/winatp-intro-fileless.txt. The device involved in these events is identified internally by Azure AD Device ID 39d8c57f-2d08-4888-b0cd-12cd0679337a.
question: According to telemetry later in the incident timeline, what is the hostname of the Windows device that these suspicious activities ultimately affected?
note: If multiple hostnames are observed, provide the one that is directly linked to the suspicious process-injection path.
solution: Suspicious process injection was observed on the host with HostName `vnevado-win11a`.

context: While analyzing an alert for unexpected behavior from a process launched without any command-line arguments communicating with the external IP 202.183.149.174, a follow-up alert titled “Suspicious process injection observed” was raised. Unexpected behavior in legitimate process: The process with ExtractedFileName `notepad.exe` was run with no command-line arguments and showed anomalous activity, suggesting it may have been the injection target.

context: During the investigation of the "Suspicious Application Window Discovery" alert triggered on July 4 2024, we noted that multiple PowerShell commands were executed on the host in quick succession (for example, process ID 7472 followed by 4656 running PowerShell with an encoded command). context: On 04 July 2024 at 22:35 UTC, Defender flagged an unexpected instance of notepad.exe running without any command-line arguments from the public IP address 202.183.149.174. This behaviour can be symptomatic of code injection or a masquerading executable. Investigators later found that, just a second earlier, a related alert titled "Suspicious Application Window Discovery" was raised on the same host, indicating that an encoded command had been executed to enumerate application windows.
question: Which executable launched the encoded command that triggered the linked "Suspicious Application Window Discovery" alert at 15:49:41 UTC on 26 June 2024?

context: On July 4th, 2024, Microsoft Defender raised an alert titled "Suspicious process injection observed." The alert showed that a file named "powershell.exe" (PID 4656) ran with an extremely long, base-64-encoded command line to bypass execution policy and fetch a remote script. This behaviour is often a precursor to code-injection into other running processes. Investigators also noted the script pulled content from an external blob-storage URL, suggesting the host might subsequently reach out to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
question: A follow-up alert reported that a process—running with no visible command-line arguments—exhibited unexpected behaviour and initiated network communication. What IP address did this process contact, according to the alert?
solution: A suspicious process injection was detected involving account with field AadUserId=`12185914-91dd-4fb9-94f9-3252203b0426`.
Subsequently, an unexpected process (run with no command-line arguments) showed abnormal behavior and communicated with IP address field Address=`202.183.149.174`.

context: On July 4, 2024, at 22:35 UTC our monitoring flagged a "Suspicious process injection observed" alert. Investigation showed that a process with command line "notepad.exe" executed after downloading content from the URL https://wcdstaticfilesprdeus.blob.core.windows.net/wcdstaticfiles/winatp-intro-fileless.txt. This behavior may indicate an attempt to hide malicious code inside a trusted process. Around the same time, another alert titled "Suspicious Application Window Discovery" was triggered on the same host, suggesting the attacker tried to enumerate windows or gather UI information for further malicious activity.
question: According to the "Suspicious Application Window Discovery" alert that followed, which executable was launched (give the process name)?
solution: A suspicious PowerShell window-discovery command was executed (entity field ProcessId__CreatedTimeUtc__CommandLine, value `4656__2024-06-26t15:49:41.4025245z__"powershell.exe" -executionpolicy bypass -encodedcommand … -inputformat xml -outputformat text`).
Soon after, a process-injection alert showed the compromised host communicating with the external IP address (entity field Address, value `72.5.72.208`).
